roadmap.goal: CI stops collecting code coverage on both stacks; Sonar's general analysis and the time-budget guard stay as they are; each stack keeps one normal and one opt-in local coverage command.

phases.name: S1 Frontend
phases.description: The guard asks about CI, then CI runs the plain tests.

steps.name: The guard asks whether it runs on CI
steps.description: A run scales its limits and never retires entries when it is a CI run or a coverage run. Rename the run kind coverage to scaled, coverageFactor to limitFactor, COVERAGE_FACTOR to LIMIT_FACTOR, and the log text to scaled run and limit factor.
criteria: CI set with no --coverage gives the run kind scaled; neither gives plain; --coverage alone gives scaled
CI set to an empty string, false or FALSE gives plain, and a run of vitest with CI=FALSE confirms Vitest reads it the same way (no bail)
A scaled run multiplies limits by the factor and never retires an entry; a plain run multiplies by 1 and retires a passed test under a quarter of the budget
The reporter prints scaled run and limit factor 3 on a scaled run

git grep -n -i coverage over the non-test guard files timeBudgetOptions.ts, compareToAllowList.ts, timeBudgetReporter.ts and vitest.config.ts returns only the --coverage argument check and the coverage settings of Vitest itself

pnpm build and the touched tests are clean in Lighthouse.Frontend; dotnet build has zero warnings when backend files changed; comments follow the project rule, with no internal references and no nWave scenario tags
steps.scenario_name: A CI run with no coverage keeps today's limits
steps.implementation_notes: DISTILL was skipped by the maintainer, so this step writes its own test rows. See the Revision section of feature-delta.md, which wins over older text. Do not revert this step alone while 01-02 stays; revert the slice.

steps.name: Frontend CI runs the plain tests; coverage becomes opt-in
steps.description: The test step runs pnpm test, sonarreport becomes test:coverage, and Sonar no longer reads lcov. One CI-shaped run proves the guard and the reports.
criteria: build-frontend/action.yml runs pnpm test; --coverage appears only in the test:coverage script
sonar-project.properties has no sonar.javascript.lcov.reportPaths; sonar.testExecutionReportPaths stays
git grep sonarreport returns nothing outside docs/feature and docs/evolution

The comment above Check test-time budget says its limits are in coverage-run seconds and looser on a plain run until they are measured on one; check_budget.py and test-time-budget.json are unchanged (git diff shows neither)
toolchain-pins.test.mjs passes

One run with CI=true and no --coverage over a planted 9 s test and a planted 5 s test: the run goes red, names the 9 s test, does not name the 5 s test, skips the stale check, and writes sonar-report.xml and test-results.json; the planted tests are removed afterwards
pnpm test:coverage over one small test file prints a coverage table; pnpm test over the same file prints none; @vitest/coverage-v8 stays in package.json
Comments name no internal references: git diff shows no T4, D1, AC or slice ids in added comment lines

pnpm build and the touched tests are clean in Lighthouse.Frontend; dotnet build has zero warnings when backend files changed; comments follow the project rule, with no internal references and no nWave scenario tags
steps.scenario_name: A plain CI-shaped run still fails a slow test
steps.implementation_notes: Step name Test Frontend and Sonar report stays. Check test-time budget, check_budget.py and test-time-budget.json are otherwise unchanged. In the ADR and the KPI contract change only the command name. That a planted fast listed test does not retire on CI is pinned at unit level in 01-01; the maintainer cut the end-to-end proof down to one manual check.

phases.name: S2 Backend
phases.description: One plain test step and a local coverage script.

steps.name: Backend CI runs without the collector; a local coverage script
steps.description: One Test Backend step with no coverage collector, no opencover settings in the scanner, and a new local script Lighthouse.Backend/Test-Coverage.ps1.
criteria: ci_backend.yml has one step named Test Backend with no if: line, with --logger trx and RunConfiguration.MaxCpuCount=0, and no --collect
git grep for opencover, XPlat Code Coverage and coverage.exclusions in .github returns nothing
sonar.cs.vstest.reportsPaths stays, and the run_sonar conditions on the Sonar steps stay
The ci.yml comment no longer says with coverage, and the comment above the backend budget step says its limits are in coverage-run seconds and looser on a plain run until they are measured on one
The comment in ForecastRealityCheckAcceptanceTest.cs no longer claims CI uses a coverage run
Test-Coverage.ps1 has CmdletBinding, ErrorActionPreference Stop and a -Filter parameter defaulting to the live-connector exclusion, and passes none of the CI-only arguments or anything after --
dotnet test --list-tests with the default filter shows no test of the live-connector categories
Test-Coverage.ps1 run once with -Filter narrowed to one small test class writes a coverage.cobertura.xml
coverlet.collector stays in the test project; actionlint reports nothing on the changed workflows

pnpm build and the touched tests are clean in Lighthouse.Frontend; dotnet build has zero warnings when backend files changed; comments follow the project rule, with no internal references and no nWave scenario tags
steps.scenario_name: The backend runs plain in CI and coverage stays available locally
steps.implementation_notes: CI filters with Category!= and CLAUDE.md with TestCategory!=; confirm the spelling chosen selects what is intended. The backend budget step stays --warn-only.

phases.name: Close
phases.description: Mutation and local gates on frozen code, then one push of both slices and the CI read.

steps.name: Mutation and full local gates on frozen code
steps.description: Stryker on timeBudgetOptions.ts, then the full local gates. One commit per slice stays, so each is a plain revert.
criteria: Stryker on timeBudgetOptions.ts reports at least 80 %, survivors killed or listed with a reason, recorded in the feature's mutation folder
pnpm test, pnpm build, dotnet build and the filtered dotnet test are green

steps.name: Push once and read CI
steps.description: On the maintainer's word, push both slices together, then check the DEVOPS verification table and read the saving as the DEVOPS section says.
criteria: Every row of the DEVOPS verification table is checked on the first main run and recorded
The saving is read from same-group runs and summed per-test seconds, and recorded with whatever runs exist
steps.implementation_notes: Lead-owned. A red run reverts or fixes the stack concerned.
